sections.title: Economic channel · Monetary policy
sections.body: Policy rates influence financing costs, asset discount rates and relative currency returns. Model assumption: Higher policy-rate changes support the currency channel; they weigh on equity, crypto and precious-metal discount-rate channels. Conditions: Markets react to expected future policy and surprises. A rate hike already priced in can coincide with a weaker currency.

sections.title: Economic channel · Inflation and wages
sections.body: Inflation and wages inform purchasing power, profit margins and the policy outlook. Model assumption: The currency model assumes higher inflation increases tightening pressure. Index and crypto models apply the discount-rate channel. Conditions: Supply shocks, stagflation and credibility concerns can reverse the currency response. High inflation is not automatically risk-on.

sections.title: Economic channel · Employment
sections.body: Employment and unemployment inform income, demand and resource slack. Model assumption: Stronger employment supports currency and earnings channels; unemployment and claims use inverse direction. Conditions: Strong jobs can also increase expected interest rates. Revisions, labour-force participation and the business cycle matter.

sections.title: Economic channel · Growth and activity
sections.body: Output and demand influence earnings, imports and industrial commodity consumption. Model assumption: Improving activity supports the currency and index earnings channels; commodity effects depend on the mapped consuming economy. Conditions: A rising PMI below 50 is improvement, not necessarily expansion. Annual and quarterly series cannot be treated as interchangeable.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: The directional reading balances released actual-versus-previous changes by independent economic theme and includes mapped positioning. Crypto additionally uses available network, issuance and chain-liquidity evidence. Historical macro series provide context and are not treated as dated release surprises. Market prices, yields and headlines are displayed as confirmation and are excluded from the official bias score.
